title: Jupyter notebook server is exposed without a token
summary: A Jupyter server is answering its authenticated API without a token or password, so anyone who can reach it can open a notebook, run code and read files on the host.  An open Jupyter server is arbitrary code execution on the machine it runs on.

confirm.control: A path that cannot exist, so the site's not found answer is known and an open API response is told apart from a soft 404.
confirm.differential: status == 200 and (body_contains("\"kernelspecs\"") or (body_contains("\"type\":\"directory\"") and body_contains("\"writable\"")) or body_contains("\"execution_state\"")) and body_differs(control)

reproduce: curl -sk 'https://host/api/contents' (or /api/kernelspecs) with no token.  A token protected server answers 403; an open one answers 200 with the contents listing (type directory, writable) or the kernel specs.  Either means the server runs code for anyone who can reach it.
remediate: Set a strong token or password, bind the server to localhost or a trusted range (c.NotebookApp.ip and c.NotebookApp.token), and firewall it off the internet.  Never run a notebook server open to the network.
